notes: Alico Inc. (NASDAQ: ALCO). Florida-based agribusiness historically focused on citrus production (Alico Citrus segment) and land management. In January 2025 management announced a strategic transformation: wind-down of citrus operations after the 2024-25 harvest and pivot to a land-development / asset-light model. Fiscal year ends September 30. Two reportable segments: Alico Citrus (revenue from oranges sold to Tropicana/Florida's Natural under multi-year supply contracts) and Land Management & Other Operations (cattle grazing, hunting leases, mining royalties, real estate). Data from SEC EDGAR (CIK 0000003545) 10-K and 10-Q filings. Net debt = total debt (mortgage + RLOC + term notes with MetLife / Rabo) less cash. EBITDA computed as operating income + D&A unless company-disclosed Adjusted EBITDA; FY24-25 results materially impacted by Hurricane Ian (Sept 2022) USDA RMA crop-insurance and FDOC-block-grant proceeds, plus citrus-greening-driven yield declines. Acreage: peak ~125k acres of land owned (consolidated), with ~48k-50k of citrus groves (now declining to zero) and balance pasture / open / ranchland.

periods.notes: FY19 (yr-end Sept 2019): revenue $122.4M dominated by Alico Citrus ($116.2M). EBITDA computed = op income + D&A. Hurricane Irma (Sept 2017) recovery still in progress.
FY20: revenue $89.6M (-27% YoY on citrus pricing weakness and reduced harvest).
Q1 FY21 (calendar Q4 2020): revenue $28.0M.
Q2 FY21: revenue $51.0M (peak harvest quarter).
Q3 FY21: revenue $18.0M. Aug 2021: completed sale of ~17,229 ranch-acre Alico Ranch parcel to State of FL for $79.6M, plus other ranch sales — material acreage reduction.
Q4 FY21: revenue $6.0M (off-season). Net income $50M+ boosted by $76M+ gain on Alico Ranch sale.
FY21: revenue $102.5M. Net income $60M boosted by $79M gain on Alico Ranch sale. Net debt cut to $73M. Special dividend $1.00 paid in early FY22.
Q1 FY22: revenue $33.5M.
Q2 FY22: revenue $50.0M (peak harvest quarter).
Q3 FY22: revenue $18.0M.
Q4 FY22: revenue $13.0M. Hurricane Ian (Sept 28, 2022) caused significant grove damage; impairment charges began.
FY22: revenue $114.5M. Hurricane Ian damage in Q4. Net loss $2M including initial impairments.
Q1 FY23: revenue $21.0M (Hurricane Ian dropped harvest yields ~50%).
Q2 FY23: revenue $35.0M; insurance proceeds beginning to flow.
Q3 FY23: revenue $17.0M.
Q4 FY23: revenue $12.0M.
FY23: revenue $85.0M (-26% YoY) due to Hurricane Ian yield reduction. Crop insurance / FDOC block grant proceeds partially offset.
Q1 FY24: revenue $12.0M.
Q2 FY24: revenue $27.0M.
Q3 FY24: revenue $13.5M.
Q4 FY24: revenue $9.0M. Large impairment charges as management prepares strategic transformation announcement; began divesting non-core ranchland.
FY24: revenue $61.5M (-28% YoY). Net loss $62M including $80M+ in impairments on citrus groves ahead of wind-down decision. Acreage cut as ranch divestitures accelerate.
Q1 FY25 (calendar Q4 2024): revenue $16.0M. January 2025 strategic transformation announced — citrus wind-down post 2024-25 harvest, pivot to land development.
Q2 FY25: revenue $19.0M (final material citrus harvest quarter).
Q3 FY25: revenue $6.5M. Citrus harvest concluding; gains on initial ranchland sales.
Q4 FY25: revenue $2.5M (post citrus wind-down). Cash built to $38M from disposition proceeds. Net debt $47.4M. Latest seed-data anchor period.

FY25: final year of citrus operations. Revenue $44M. EBITDA $22.5M including realized gains on initial ranch dispositions. Pivot to land development underway. Market value of ~49.5k acres of ranchland and former groves estimated $686M (per third-party / management commentary on H&H valuation).
